comments.body:
**(Significant) `file-size-limit.sh` will produce ~47 first-run violations but §3.4 documents zero.**

I ran `find crates/bm/src/ -name '*.rs' -exec wc -l {} +` and counted **47 files exceeding 300 lines**. Top offenders in domain modules:

| File | Lines |
|------|-------|
| profile/extraction.rs | 1508 |
| workspace/repo.rs | 1287 |
| web/files.rs | 1102 |
| profile/mod.rs | 1003 |
| daemon/api.rs | 997 |
| brain/bridge_adapter.rs | 985 |
| formation/mod.rs | 729 |
| brain/event_watcher.rs | 696 |
| ... | (32 more domain files) |

Plus 5 files in commands/ (init.rs:939, completions.rs:575, debug.rs:412, brain_run.rs:338, profiles_init.rs:331), cli.rs (786), and main.rs (307).

§3.4 exhaustively documents domain-layer-imports.sh (9 violations, per-file table) and no-hardcoded-profiles.sh (74 violations, per-file table). Yet file-size-limit.sh — which produces *more first-run output than any other check* — has zero documentation in §3.4.

An agent seeing ~47 VIOLATION messages with no baseline context would either waste cycles investigating each one or lose trust in the check system entirely. The whole purpose of §3.4 is to set expectations about first-run output.

Also: the exclusion list says "Excludes target/, test fixtures" but never mentions commands/. The check scans ALL of `crates/bm/src/` including commands/. Should it? If so, document the full 47-file baseline. If not, add commands/ to the exclusion list and document the ~40-file domain-only baseline.

**(Moderate) `test-path-isolation.sh` will false-positive on doc comment at integration.rs:6.**

The grep for `dirs::home_dir()` in `crates/bm/tests/` will match this line:

```
crates/bm/tests/integration.rs:6://! config via `dirs::home_dir()` are invoked as subprocesses with per-test HOME.
```

This is a doc comment (`//!`), not a function call. The grep pattern matches the text regardless of context. So the check will report 1 violation in tests/ on first run — a false positive.

The design should either:
1. Acknowledge this as a known false positive in the first-run violations section
2. Specify that the grep excludes comment lines (e.g., `grep -v '^\s*//'` post-filter)
3. Note that `// check:ignore` can suppress it

Currently the design says nothing about test-path-isolation.sh first-run output, implying 0 violations in tests/ — which is incorrect.
